value.name: name
value.value: GRIP ADM Detector \[Ablated Diffusion\]
value.description: Name of the model.

value.name: description
value.value: A convolutional detector that classifies images as real or fully synthetic. It is optimized for images generated by the Ablated Diffusion Model (ADM) and similar diffusion architectures. The architecture is a ResNet-50 variant with an initial residual-extraction layer and no downsampling in the first layer, which helps preserve the subtle high-frequency traces left by the generation process. The model is trained from scratch on ADM images with strong augmentation (blurring, JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, geometric transformations, cut-out, and brightness and contrast changes) to make it more robust to the processing images undergo on social networks. It may also flag images from other generative models, but performance outside the ADM family is not guaranteed.
value.description: Model introduction, purpose, capabilities, novelty and caveats.

value.name: instructions
value.value:
1\. Create the environment from environment.yml (or install PyTorch and the listed dependencies).

2\. Load the ADM checkpoint into the ResNet-50 variant (with the residual-extraction layer and no downsampling in the first layer).

3\. Feed images at their original resolution. Do not resize or crop them, because resampling can erase the high-frequency traces the detector relies on.

4\. Apply the same normalization used in training. \[Confirm for your checkpoint.\]

5\. Read the output score and compare it to a decision threshold.

6\. For best accuracy on a new image source, calibrate the threshold using a few known real and synthetic samples from that source.
value.description: Use instructions.

value.name: inputs_outputs
value.value:
Input: a single RGB image (PNG or JPEG), any resolution, without resizing.

Output: a single scalar score per image.

value.value: Performance depends mainly on the generator architecture, post-processing such as compression and resizing, file format, decision threshold calibration, image content and resolution, and adversarial attempts to remove generation traces.

value.name: more
value.value: Outputs are most reliable on images whose origin and processing resemble the training conditions. When the model is applied to a new image source, the decision threshold should be calibrated on a few known real and synthetic samples from that source, and the model should be re-evaluated regularly as new generators appear. Combining it with detectors trained on other generators improves coverage.

value.name: datasets
value.value: Synthetic images generated by ADM (Ablated Diffusion Model, Dhariwal and Nichol, 2021), labelled as synthetic, together with real images labelled as pristine.
value.description: Dataset(s) used during training.

value.name: motivation
value.value: ADM was chosen because it is among the hardest generators to detect: its images leave much weaker spectral traces than GANs and other diffusion models, and detectors trained on ProGAN or Latent Diffusion images perform poorly on it. Training directly on ADM images is meant to fill this gap and improve detection of ADM and architecturally similar diffusion models.
value.description: Why were training datasets chosen?

value.name: preprocessing
value.value: The model is trained from scratch, without pretraining, using strong data augmentation: blurring, JPEG compression, Gaussian noise addition, geometric transformations, cut-out, and brightness and contrast changes. These augmentations simulate the processing images undergo when shared online, such as on social networks, and make the detector more robust to it.

value.name: datasets
value.value: Real images from COCO, ImageNet and UCID. Synthetic images from 12 generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN2, StyleGAN3, BigGAN, EG3D, Taming Transformers, DALL·E Mini, DALL·E 2, GLIDE, Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion and ADM. Text-to-image models were prompted with captions from the COCO training and validation sets. Each generator contributes 1,000 synthetic images, which are compared against 5,000 real images.
value.description: Dataset(s) used during evaluation.

value.name: motivation
value.value: The evaluation set was chosen to measure how well detectors generalize to architectures not seen in training and how robust they are to realistic processing. It covers GANs, transformer-based models and diffusion models, including both class-conditional and text-to-image generators, while the real images include JPEG-compressed photographs (COCO, ImageNet) and uncompressed images (UCID).
value.description: Why were evaluation datasets chosen?

value.name: preprocessing
value.value: Two test settings are used. In the uncompressed setting, synthetic images are tested in the PNG format in which they were generated. In the resized and compressed setting, which simulates social-network processing and follows the IEEE VIP Cup 2022 protocol, a crop of random large size and position is taken from every test image, real or synthetic, resized to 200×200 pixels, and JPEG-compressed with a random quality factor between 65 and 100. A CSV file distributed with the test set records the processing applied to each image.
value.description: Data pre-processing for evaluation (tokenizer, data augmentation etc.).

value.name: more
value.value: The synthetic test images and the processing CSV are publicly available from the GRIP repository ([https://github.com/grip-unina/DMimageDetection](https://github.com/grip-unina/DMimageDetection)); the real images must be downloaded separately from COCO, ImageNet and UCID. The COCO captions used as prompts are licensed under CC BY 4.0. In the uncompressed setting, real images carry JPEG artifacts while synthetic images do not, which can make detection appear easier than it is in practice.
value.description: Additional evaluation set information not found above.

value.name: analysis
value.value: Diffusion models leave very different forensic traces: GLIDE, Latent Diffusion and Stable Diffusion show clear spectral peaks similar to GANs, while ADM and DALL·E 2 show much weaker ones and are the hardest to detect. Detectors trained on one generator perform well on generators with similar artifacts but poorly on others. In the resized and compressed setting, AUC often remains acceptable on unseen generators, but accuracy at a fixed threshold drops close to chance. Fusing detectors trained on different generators and calibrating the threshold on a few samples substantially improves accuracy, although images whose artifacts differ strongly from those seen in training remain difficult to detect.
value.description: Analysis and explanation of performance results.

value.name: thresholds
value.value: A fixed threshold of 0.5 on the output probability (a logit of 0 when a sigmoid is applied) is used by default, as in the reference paper, since it is the natural decision boundary of the binary classifier. The paper shows that this threshold is often poorly suited to generators and image sources not seen in training, where accuracy can fall close to 50% even when AUC is high. Calibrating the threshold with Platt scaling, using as few as two real and two synthetic images per generator, raised average accuracy from 64.5% to 87.8% in the paper's fusion experiment, so calibration on the target image source is recommended.
value.description: If decision thresholds are used, what are they, and why were those parameters chosen?

value.name: methodology
value.value: Each generator is evaluated on 1,000 synthetic images against 5,000 real images. Two metrics are computed per generator: the area under the ROC curve (AUC), which does not depend on a threshold, and accuracy at the fixed threshold of 0.5. Results are averaged across the 12 generators with a simple mean, in both the uncompressed and the resized and compressed settings. No confidence intervals or other uncertainty measures are reported.
value.description: Explanation of how metrics are calculated and averaged, with uncertainty measures and evaluation method.

value.name: ethics
value.value: The evaluation uses public datasets such as COCO and ImageNet that include photographs of people, used under the datasets' terms. In use, false positives can unfairly damage the credibility of photographers, sources or news outlets, while false negatives can lend credibility to synthetic content. Recommended mitigations are keeping a human expert in the loop, reporting results with their uncertainty, combining the model with other verification evidence, and never using it as the sole basis for decisions about individuals

value.name: risks
value.value: Design faults: limited generalization means the model can miss images from generators whose artifacts differ from ADM, and a fixed threshold can be badly miscalibrated on new image sources. Technical faults: resizing, cropping or strong compression of inputs, including by preprocessing pipelines, can erase the traces the detector depends on. Environmental threats: generators evolve quickly, so the model becomes less reliable over time, and adversaries can deliberately remove or mask generation traces to evade detection. Possible consequences include synthetic images being accepted as authentic, contributing to disinformation, and authentic images being wrongly flagged as synthetic.
value.description: Possible threats to the model's validity (design and technical faults) and consequences.

value.name: security
value.value: The model is not certified for cybersecurity, and no compliance with specific security standards is reported. Its robustness to adversarial attacks has not been evaluated.
value.description: Is the model certified for cybersecurity or is it compliant with specific security standards?

value.name: caveats
value.value: The model was developed and evaluated in a research setting, and no validation for production deployment is documented. Its performance on current generators is unknown and should be measured before use. Because the first layer does not downsample and images are processed at full resolution, memory and compute requirements are higher than for a standard ResNet-50 and grow with image size.
value.description: Additional concerns that were not covered in the previous sections.
